statementWrapper.draftTooltip: A Draft is a flexible statement that converts to Action or Group after execution. Use this when you're not sure if your instruction will need one or multiple steps. After execution, it automatically becomes an Action (single step) or Group (multiple steps) based on what the AI produces. (Ctrl+Alt+B)
statementWrapper.draftInstruction1: A Draft is a flexible statement that converts after execution.
statementWrapper.draftInstruction2: If the AI produces one action, it becomes an Action.
statementWrapper.draftInstruction3: If the AI produces multiple actions, it becomes a Group.
statementWrapper.draftInstruction4: Use this when you're not sure how many steps your instruction will need.
statementWrapper.actionTooltip: An Action performs interactions with the page using natural language descriptions. Examples: "Click the submit button", "Fill in the email field with user@example.com", "Select California from the state dropdown". The AI agent interprets your description and executes the appropriate browser action. (Ctrl+Alt+A)
statementWrapper.actionInstruction1: An Action performs interactions with the page using natural language descriptions.
statementWrapper.actionInstruction2: The AI agent interprets your description and executes the appropriate browser action.
statementWrapper.actionInstruction3: Examples: "Click the first search result", "Scroll to the reviews section", "Wait for the page to load"
statementWrapper.assertionTooltip: An Assertion verifies that something on the page matches your expectations. Examples: "The page title should contain Welcome", "The error message should be visible", "The cart total should be $99.99". Tests will fail if assertions are not met. (Ctrl+Alt+T)
statementWrapper.assertionInstruction1: An Assertion verifies that something on the page matches your expectations.
statementWrapper.assertionInstruction2: Tests will fail if assertions are not met.
statementWrapper.assertionInstruction3: Examples: "The page title should contain Welcome", "The error message should be visible", "The cart total should be $99.99"
statementWrapper.editInstruction1: Edit this statement's configuration, description, or parameters.
statementWrapper.editInstruction2: For actions and assertions, you can modify the natural language description.
statementWrapper.editInstruction3: For code blocks, edit the JavaScript directly.
statementWrapper.duplicateTooltip: Duplicate this statement and all its contents. Useful for creating similar actions with minor variations or repeating patterns. The copy will be inserted immediately after this statement.
statementWrapper.duplicateInstruction1: Duplicate this statement and all its contents.
statementWrapper.duplicateInstruction2: Useful for creating similar actions with minor variations or repeating patterns.
statementWrapper.duplicateInstruction3: The copy will be inserted immediately after this statement.
statementWrapper.deleteTooltip: Delete this statement permanently. For containers like Steps or If/Else blocks, this will also delete all nested statements. Use Ctrl+Alt+D for quick deletion. (Ctrl+Alt+D)
statementWrapper.deleteInstruction1: Permanently removes this statement from the test case.
statementWrapper.deleteInstruction2: For containers like Steps or If/Else blocks, this will also delete all nested statements.
statementWrapper.codeTooltip: Code blocks execute custom JavaScript directly in the browser context. Use for complex logic, data manipulation, or operations not easily expressed in natural language. Examples: calculating values, parsing JSON, setting cookies, or interacting with browser APIs. Code has access to the page object and all Playwright APIs. (Ctrl+Alt+C)
statementWrapper.codeInstruction1: Code blocks execute custom JavaScript directly in the browser context.
statementWrapper.codeInstruction2: Use for complex logic, data manipulation, or operations not easily expressed in natural language.
statementWrapper.codeInstruction3: The code has access to the page object and can use await for async operations.
statementWrapper.codeInstruction4: Examples: Calculate values, parse JSON, set cookies, or interact with browser APIs.
statementWrapper.functionTooltip: Functions are reusable test components that accept parameters. Use them to avoid duplicating common sequences like login flows, form submissions, or navigation patterns. Example: A "Login" function with username and password parameters can be reused across multiple tests. (Ctrl+Alt+F)
statementWrapper.functionInstruction1: Functions are reusable test components that accept parameters.
statementWrapper.functionInstruction2: Use them to avoid duplicating common sequences like login flows, form submissions, or navigation patterns.
statementWrapper.functionInstruction3: Examples: A "Login" function with username and password parameters can be reused across multiple tests.
statementWrapper.uploadFileTooltip: Upload File actions attach files from your Test Data library to file input elements on the page. First upload files in the Test Data section, then select them here. Useful for testing file uploads, document processing, or image submissions. The action automatically handles file input elements and drag-and-drop zones. (Ctrl+Alt+U)
statementWrapper.uploadFileInstruction1: Upload File actions attach files from your Test Data library to file input elements on the page.
statementWrapper.uploadFileInstruction2: First upload files in the Test Data section, then select them here.
statementWrapper.uploadFileInstruction3: Useful for testing file uploads, document processing, or image submissions.
statementWrapper.uploadFileInstruction4: The action automatically handles file input elements and drag-and-drop zones.
statementWrapper.extractTooltip: Extract actions capture content from the page and save it to variables for later use. Examples: "Extract the order confirmation number and save to orderNumber", "Extract the user ID from the profile page and save to userId". These variables can be referenced in subsequent actions using $variableName syntax. (Ctrl+Alt+E)
statementWrapper.extractInstruction1: Extract actions capture content from the page and save it to variables for later use.
statementWrapper.extractInstruction2: These variables can be referenced in subsequent actions using $variableName syntax.
statementWrapper.extractInstruction3: Examples: "Extract the order confirmation number and save to orderNumber", "Extract the user ID from the profile page and save to userId".
statementWrapper.waitUntilTooltip: Wait for a specific condition to be met before continuing. Use natural language to describe what to wait for, like "The loading spinner disappears" or "The success message appears". Set a maximum timeout to prevent tests from hanging. (Ctrl+Alt+W)
statementWrapper.waitUntilInstruction1: Wait for a specific condition to be met before continuing.
statementWrapper.waitUntilInstruction2: Use natural language to describe what to wait for.
statementWrapper.waitUntilInstruction3: Examples: "The loading spinner disappears", "The success message appears".
statementWrapper.waitUntilInstruction4: Set a maximum timeout to prevent tests from hanging.
statementWrapper.groupTooltip: Groups are logical containers that organize related actions together. Use them to structure your test into meaningful sections like "User Registration", "Checkout Process", or "Search and Filter". Groups can be collapsed/expanded and help with test readability and maintenance. (Ctrl+Alt+G)
statementWrapper.groupInstruction1: Groups are logical containers that organize related actions together.
statementWrapper.groupInstruction2: Use them to structure your test into meaningful sections like "User Registration", "Checkout Process", or "Search and Filter".
statementWrapper.groupInstruction3: Groups can be collapsed/expanded and help with test readability and maintenance.
statementWrapper.templateTooltip: Templates are pre-defined step groups. Convert this statement to a template reference, then select a template to auto-populate common test patterns like login, navigation, or form submission. (Ctrl+Alt+R)
statementWrapper.templateInstruction1: Templates reference pre-defined step groups for common test patterns.
statementWrapper.templateInstruction2: After conversion, select a template to auto-populate actions.
statementWrapper.templateInstruction3: Examples: login flow, navigation, form submission, data verification.
statementWrapper.templateInstruction4: Helps maintain consistency across tests and reduces duplication.
statementWrapper.extractEmailContentTooltip: Extract specific content from emails like verification codes, activation links, or custom data. Configure filters to target emails from specific senders, with specific subjects, or containing certain text. The extracted content is automatically saved as a variable for use in subsequent test steps.
statementWrapper.extractEmailContentInstruction1: Extract specific content from emails like verification codes or activation links.
statementWrapper.extractEmailContentInstruction2: Configure filters to target emails from specific senders or with specific subjects.
statementWrapper.extractEmailContentInstruction3: Set custom prompts to guide the extraction process.
statementWrapper.extractEmailContentInstruction4: Extracted content is automatically saved as a variable for use in subsequent steps.
statementWrapper.ifElseTooltip: If/Else statements execute different actions based on conditions. The condition can be JavaScript code or natural language. Example: "If the user is logged in" then perform checkout actions, else show login form. Useful for handling different states, A/B tests, or dynamic content. (Ctrl+Alt+I)
statementWrapper.ifElseInstruction1: If/Else statements execute different actions based on conditions.
statementWrapper.ifElseInstruction2: The condition can be JavaScript code or natural language.
statementWrapper.ifElseInstruction3: Examples: "If the user is logged in" then perform checkout actions, else show login form.
statementWrapper.loopTooltip: While loops repeat a set of actions as long as a condition is true. Examples: "While there are more pages" click next and extract data, "While the loading spinner is visible" wait. Use for pagination, polling for changes, or processing lists of unknown length. Include a maximum iteration limit to prevent infinite loops. (Ctrl+Alt+L)
statementWrapper.loopInstruction1: While loops repeat a set of actions as long as a condition is true.
statementWrapper.loopInstruction2: The condition is checked before each iteration.
statementWrapper.loopInstruction3: Examples: "While there are more pages" click next and extract data, "While the loading spinner is visible" wait.
